<edits>
component: harness.py
candidates: dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3
change: Added code block extraction via regex pattern ```python\n(.*?)\n``` and execution through tools.python(), with fallback to text extraction if no code block is found. All 8 candidates applied identical modification.
observed: Base rollouts (base1, base2, base3) diverged on the same deterministic input (producing 52, 44, 35 one bits respectively), each with LLM text assertions of different hallucinated values for 91^14 (52,201,161,903,975,951 vs. 52036560683937853451 vs. 6,333,235,982,093,589,971). All 8 editing candidates extracted and executed Python code blocks deterministically, converging to 45 (e.g., dom1 rollout shows [python] execution block with output "91^14 = 2670419511272061205254504361" and "Number of 1 bits (using bit_count): 45"). inv1, which retained base harness, fell back to text extraction and returned 46.
verdict: confounded

component: prompts/task.md
candidates: dom1, inv2, dom2, inv3, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3
change: Added explicit instruction "Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer." All 8 candidates applied identical modification.
observed: Base rollouts and inv1 (with bare question prompt) show LLM generating code in varied formats (bash function_calls wrappers, XML tags, inline text) or performing pure reasoning without markdown ```python``` code blocks. All 8 editing candidates with added instruction show LLM generating ```python\n...\n``` markdown code blocks (agg2 rollout shows LLM producing ```python code block, which harness extracts and executes deterministically). Instruction directly triggers markdown-formatted code generation that matches extraction regex pattern.
verdict: confounded

component: prompts/system.md
candidates: all candidates
change: None—all candidates retained "You are a helpful assistant."
observed: No trajectory differences attributable to system prompt variation.
verdict: no observed effect
</edits>

<experience>
cue: A deterministic computational problem where the base harness diverges across runs due to unaided LLM reasoning, with different final answers each traced to hallucinated intermediate values in text assertions (e.g., LLM computing different decimal values for the same exponentiation).

lesson: When a deterministic computation task shows divergent outputs in base due to LLM text assertion (not code execution), apply code extraction and explicit code-generation instruction to the harness as a pair: in harness.py, add regex extraction of ```python\n(.*?)\n``` code blocks with execution via tools.python() and fallback to text if none found; in prompts/task.md, add explicit instruction requesting Python code generation. Both components are necessary together: extraction without instruction leaves no code blocks for the harness to extract (LLM performs manual text reasoning); instruction without extraction leaves code blocks unexecuted (LLM generates code but harness ignores it). Together, they shift the answer from stochastic LLM text assertion to deterministic code execution.

evidence: Edit rows "harness.py extraction + execution" and "prompts/task.md instruction" are confounded—all 8 editing candidates (dom1-3, inv2, inv3, agg1-3) applied both changes together. All 8 converged to 45 via code execution (rollouts show [python] execution blocks with deterministic output 91^14 = 2670419511272061205254504361, bit_count(): 45). Base and inv1 (both without extraction, inv1 also without instruction) diverged (52, 44, 35) or returned incorrect text assertions. This task's record does not isolate components; necessity of both rests on library evidence cited in decision documents (inv2.md, dom2.md, inv3.md, dom3.md cite holdout-numeric-005, which explicitly isolates components: extraction without instruction → no code blocks generated, fallback to text, divergence persists; instruction without extraction → code blocks generated but not executed, divergence persists; both together → deterministic execution, convergence). Library pattern documented across four independent tasks (holdout-numeric-002, 003, 005, 010) all triggering on this cue and all applying identical two-component solution.

confidence: medium—uniform convergence to correct answer (45) across all editing candidates is strong; library precedent is rigorous and directly applicable to this problem type; but components are confounded in this task's own record, so lesson rests partly on cross-task library isolation (holdout-numeric-005) rather than isolation within this task's execution.
</experience>
